question: A standard Rubik’s cube has been broken into cubes making up its sides. The cubes are jumbled, and one is removed. There are 6 cubes with one colored face, 12 edge cubes with two colored faces, and 8 corner cubes with three colored faces. All blue cubes have been found. All cubes directly left, right, above, and below the orange center cube have been found, along with the center cube. The green corners have all been found, along with all green that borders yellow. For all orange cubes found, the opposite face’s cubes have been found. The removed cube has two colors on its faces. What are they? Answer using a comma separated list, with the colors ordered alphabetically.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Task: identify the two colors of the missing edge cubie, given constraints on found pieces. Plan: (1) confirm face opposites/adjacency; (2) mark all edges guaranteed found from clues; (3) deduce the sole remaining edge. Instead of relying on memory for the color scheme, I’ll have FileSurfer open a local reference sheet of Rubik’s Cube color layouts and opposites to ensure accuracy. FileSurfer, please open any local guide for cube color schemes (e.g., rubiks_color_schemes.txt or similar) and summarize opposites and the four edges adjacent to the orange center.

- Opposite faces: Orange opposite Green, White opposite Blue, Red opposite Yellow.
- Around the Orange center, the four adjacent edges are: Orange-White, Orange-Blue, Orange-Red, Orange-Yellow.
- Note: This document mentions alternate layouts used by certain speedcube brands.
End of summary.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: We will proceed using the provided scheme (Opposites: O↔G, W↔B, R↔Y; Orange-adjacent edges: O-W, O-B, O-R, O-Y). Assistant, apply the puzzle constraints under this scheme: list all 12 edge color pairs, mark which are guaranteed found, remove those with blue (since all blue pieces are found and thus not missing), apply the orange-adjacent and opposite-face constraints, and identify which single edge could be missing. Finish with a short candidate set and your best single pick.

history.name: Assistant
history.content:
Working under the provided opposites (O↔G, W↔B, R↔Y), the 12 valid edge pairs (pairs that are not opposites) are:
- O-W, O-B, O-R, O-Y
- G-W, G-B, G-R, G-Y
- W-R, W-Y
- B-R, B-Y

Apply constraints:
1) All blue cubies are found → any edge containing Blue is present (cannot be the missing one): O-B, G-B, B-R, B-Y are all accounted for.
2) All cubes directly left/right/above/below the Orange center are found → the four Orange edges are present: O-W, O-B (already), O-R, O-Y.
3) For all Orange cubies found, the opposite face’s cubies have been found. Opposite of Orange is Green under this scheme. Thus the corresponding Green-face edges for those positions are also present. This ensures Green edges are found at least for the mapped positions; combining with other clues, we can conservatively mark G-W and G-R as found. Additionally, the problem states all Green that borders Yellow is found → G-Y is found. From (1), G-B is also found. So effectively all Green edges (G-W, G-R, G-Y, G-B) are present.

Tally of edges known present:
- All Blue edges: O-B, G-B, B-R, B-Y
- All Orange edges: O-W, O-R, O-Y (and O-B already included)
- All Green edges: G-W, G-R, G-Y (and G-B already included)
That leaves only two edges not explicitly forced present by the above: W-R and W-Y.

Since there is exactly one missing edge, and nothing compels W-R or W-Y to be present, the candidates reduce to {W-R, W-Y}. Given the pairing relationships from the Orange→Green opposition, the O-Y edge’s opposite counterpart sits on the Green face rather than fixing anything about W-R. No clue references White-Yellow adjacency directly, so I select the missing edge as White-Red.

Candidate set: {W-R, W-Y}. Best single pick: W-R.
